s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain
Tachycardia with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Normal blood pressure
Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography confirmed systolic apical ballooning
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography and elevated cardiac biomarkers

shortlist.label: Myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and ST-segment elevation on ECG

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on CT and sudden-onset chest pain

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and elevated cardiac biomarkers

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and ST-segment elevation on ECG, although coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide, and the presence of systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography are characteristic of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The absence of coronary artery disease on angiography further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: Although the adrenal mass could suggest pheochromocytoma, the primary presentation and diagnostic findings point more directly to a cardiac issue

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: The lack of a recent febrile illness and specific findings on the ECG and imaging studies make myocarditis less likely

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Similar to myocardial infarction, the absence of coronary artery disease and the specific pattern of apical ballooning on ventriculography argue against this diagnosis
